cohort: The study included 100 late-pregnancy patients with oligohydramnios, divided into two groups of 50 each using propensity score matching.
finding: Oxytocin combined with amniotomy improved the induction success rate, resulted in better cervical ripening (lower CAS), and led to higher neonatal Apgar scores compared to amniotomy alone in patients with late-pregnancy oligohydramnios.
